summary: Salicylic acid is a topical beta-hydroxy acid keratolytic available over the counter for treating acne, common and plantar warts, calluses and corns, psoriasis, and seborrheic dermatitis (dandruff). It softens and loosens the outer layer of skin (keratin) to promote shedding. OTC acne products contain about 0.5-2% and wart/corn/callus removers contain about 12-40%. It is for external use only. Extensive application over large areas or prolonged use - especially in children, on broad surfaces, or under occlusion - can lead to systemic absorption and salicylate toxicity (salicylism). It should not be applied to moles, birthmarks, or irritated/infected skin, and wart/corn removers should not be used by people with diabetes or poor circulation.

moa: Salicylic acid is a keratolytic that solubilizes the intercellular cement (desmosomal/corneocyte adhesion) of the stratum corneum, reducing keratinocyte cohesion and promoting shedding (desquamation) of the outer skin layer. This softens and removes hyperkeratotic tissue such as scale, callus, and the keratin plug of acne and helps unblock pores. It also has mild anti-inflammatory and comedolytic effects.

preg: Topical salicylic acid applied to small areas is expected to result in minimal systemic absorption and low risk. However, extensive or prolonged use should be avoided in pregnancy, and patients should ask a health professional before using more than limited amounts.
lact: Limited small-area topical use is generally considered acceptable during breastfeeding. Avoid applying salicylic acid to the breast or nipple area to prevent infant ingestion, and avoid extensive application.
renal: Limited topical use over small areas does not require dose adjustment. With extensive or prolonged application, systemic salicylate absorption can occur and should be used cautiously in renal impairment.
hepatic: Limited topical use over small areas does not require dose adjustment. With extensive or prolonged application, systemic salicylate absorption can occur and should be used cautiously in hepatic impairment.

missed: If you miss an application of a scheduled topical regimen, apply it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next application; do not apply extra to make up for a missed dose. Many products are used as needed - resume your usual routine.
overdose: Overdose from topical use is uncommon but can occur with extensive application, especially over large areas, under occlusion, or in children, leading to systemic salicylate toxicity (salicylism): rapid breathing/hyperventilation, tinnitus, hearing loss, confusion, nausea, vomiting, lethargy, and in severe cases metabolic acidosis. If toxicity is suspected, remove the product, wash the skin, and seek medical care or contact a Poison Control Center; management is supportive with attention to fluids, electrolytes, and acid-base balance. Accidental ingestion should be treated as salicylate poisoning.
